paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God cares how power gets used. In this psalm, God presides over the divine assembly and asks, "How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked?" (Psalm 82:2). Then He says what they should do instead: "Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed" (Psalm 82:3). Anybody with any say over anybody else is answering to Him.

Now look at what happens when they don't. The psalm says "all the foundations of the earth are shaken" (Psalm 82:5). I think that tells us unfair judging is no small thing, because the whole earth feels it. God had said, "You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High," but then comes that little word: "But like mortals you will die, and like rulers you will fall" (Psalm 82:6-7). Big titles don't make anybody bigger than the One who gave them.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Whatever say you have, at work, at home or anywhere else, use it for the weak and the needy. And when the world feels unfair, the psalm ends where you can end too: "Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance" (Psalm 82:8). He is the true Judge, and every nation belongs to Him. I'm a stamper who got pulled out of a drawer, and I'm telling you, that is a Judge worth trusting!
